### Migrate from `FastMCP.as_proxy()` to `create_proxy()`

Source: https://github.com/prefecthq/fastmcp/blob/main/docs/getting-started/upgrading/from-fastmcp-2.mdx

Replace `FastMCP.as_proxy()` with `create_proxy()` for creating proxy instances. Note that the `backend` keyword argument was renamed to `target` in the new API.

```python
# Removed in v4
proxy = FastMCP.as_proxy("http://example.com/mcp")
proxy = FastMCP.as_proxy(backend="http://example.com/mcp")  # keyword form
```

```python
# New
from fastmcp.server import create_proxy
proxy = create_proxy("http://example.com/mcp")
proxy = create_proxy(target="http://example.com/mcp")  # as_proxy(backend=X) "u2192" create_proxy(target=X)
```

### Adding Middleware to a Proxy Server

Source: https://github.com/prefecthq/fastmcp/blob/main/fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/server.py

Shows how to add custom middleware to a proxy using add_middleware().

```python
from fastmcp.server import create_proxy
from fastmcp.server.middleware import Middleware, MiddlewareContext, CallNext
from fastmcp import FastMCP

class MetricsMiddleware(Middleware):
    async def on_call_tool(self, context: MiddlewareContext, call_next: CallNext):
        tool_name = context.params.name
        return await call_next(context)

original_server = FastMCP("MyServer")
proxy = create_proxy(original_server)
proxy.add_middleware(MetricsMiddleware())
```

### Initialize FastMCP Client with In-memory Transport

Source: https://github.com/prefecthq/fastmcp/blob/main/docs/clients/client.mdx

Use the in-memory transport for testing and development to connect directly to a FastMCP server instance within the same Python process, eliminating network and subprocess complexity.

```python
from fastmcp import Client, FastMCP

server = FastMCP("TestServer")
client = Client(server)  # In-memory, no network or subprocess
```

### In-Memory Transport Example

Source: https://github.com/prefecthq/fastmcp/blob/main/docs/clients/transports.mdx

Demonstrates connecting to a FastMCP server instance within the same Python process using in-memory transport.

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP, Client
import os

mcp = FastMCP("TestServer")

@mcp.tool
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    prefix = os.environ.get("GREETING_PREFIX", "Hello")
    return f"{prefix}, {name}!"

client = Client(mcp)

async with client:
    result = await client.call_tool("greet", {"name": "World"})
```
